limits:
WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that `list` still names a FILE-LANE collision when the same pair also trips the same/nested-worktree arm. Both cases are two LIVE roles in one repo declaring a lane; the only difference between them is whether the declared paths intersect. Role A's cwd is a projects parent that nests over role B's worktree in BOTH cases, so the worktree arm fires in both and the file-lane arm is the only thing that can distinguish them.

WHY IT EXISTS. report_overlap is an elif chain - one warning per pair - and the worktree arm sits above the file-lane arm. That precedence is right when the nesting is real. It was also applied to the nesting `cwd_is_shared_parent` already identifies as an ARTEFACT of registering before a worktree exists, whose own comment claimed such a false positive 'never changes a verdict'. It changed this one: it silenced the file-lane arm for the pair. And because the #683 lane-less exemption requires an EMPTY file lane, declaring the lane you were granted is what loses you the exemption - so declaring a lane made collision detection strictly WORSE than declaring nothing, at the moment a lane is handed over. Observed in production: an orchestrator granted docs/scripts.md to three roles at once and told a worker two files were free while another held them.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH. Nothing about whether the WORKTREE arm is right - that is asserted in tests/test_flow_wave_registry.py, which pins that a genuine nested pair is still reported. Nothing about claim-derived rows, which take a different path into the same predicate. And nothing about a pair whose repos differ: the file-lane arm is scoped to same-repo pairs by design, so this control cannot see the #800 unscoped-lane case at all.

THE CASES NAME NO ANSWER. Each case directory holds a registry.json and nothing else, generated by running the real `register`. The runner greps for the gate's own warning text, never for a role or a path, so a blind gate finds nothing.

anchors.why: The gate as it stood before #1190, vendored from d3f474b - a real ancestor, so nothing had to be constructed. MEASURED against both cases: it exits 0 on the BAD case and 0 on the GOOD one, reporting the file-lane collision in neither. It does not merely miss the finding; it answers IDENTICALLY on inputs that differ, which is the whole point of committing it. A control that only ran against the fixed gate would show two greens and could not tell you whether they came from an instrument that looked or one that could not.
